title: Where the Arm Loses a Direction: Singular Values, Three Kinds of Singularity, and a Line Drawn Over the Shoulder

questions.question: What does a smallest singular value of zero mean?
options: The tool cannot move in one direction however the joints turn
A joint has reached its limit
The tool is at the edge of the reach, and nowhere else
The Jacobian has more columns than rows
questions.explanation: The singular values are the gains from joint rates to tool velocity, direction by direction. A gain of zero is a direction no joint motion can produce.

questions.question: In a generic pose the smallest singular value was:
options: Exactly zero
questions.explanation: Away from singularities the worst direction still had a gain of 0.172. It fell smoothly toward zero as joint 5 approached zero: 0.1337, 0.0313, 0.00317.

questions.question: Passing 0.01 m from the shoulder axis, joint 1's peak rate was, undamped and damped:
options: 2.0 and 26.1 rad/s
26.1 rad/s for both
26.1 and 2.0 rad/s
0.25 and 2.0 rad/s
questions.explanation: Passing a centimetre from the shoulder's axis asks joint 1 for half a turn in an instant. Damped as the singular value falls, the same pass asked 2.0 rad/s.

questions.question: What did the damped pass cost?
options: Nothing: the tool stayed on the line
A longer pass, on the same line
A joint driven into its limit
The tool strayed 0.0448 m from the line, against 0.0006 m
questions.explanation: A step that refuses the impossible direction lets the tool leave the line by 0.0448 m, where the exact one kept it to 0.0006 m and could not be driven.

questions.question: Why is the smallest singular value only a number you choose to read?
options: It changes with the pose
It mixes metres and radians
It is only known to a few digits
It is the same for every arm
questions.explanation: Its size depends on how the rows are scaled. Three rows of the Jacobian are in metres per radian and three are pure numbers. Weight the rotation differently and the same pose gives another value.

questions.question: What is better than damping through a singularity?
options: More damping
A slower tool speed everywhere
Switching to joint space at the last moment
Planning so as not to go near it
questions.explanation: Damping is what to do when the arm is already there. A planner that keeps the singular value over a floor, or picks the other wrist solution, never has to.
